Layer-wise analysis is too coarse and misses local variations,
while channel-wise or group-wise mixed precision is imprac-
tical on conventional systolic arrays because it would require
multiple bit-widths to coexist simultaneously within a single
tile, disrupting its uniform dataflow and hardware regularity.
Sensitivity-Guided Mixed-Precision Allocation.The
ranked sensitivity profile directly determines how bit-widths
are assigned across channel windows, prioritizing those with
the largest perplexity impact. The allocation is parameterized
by a baseline precisionb low, a target upper precisionb high,
and a desired average precisionb virt that defines the overall
precision budget. Here,b virt serves as the virtual precision,
a fractional mean bit-width that characterizes the model’s
effective average precision. The mixed-precision configuration
is obtained by upgrading the most sensitive channel windows
fromb low towardb high until the model’s weighted mean preci-
sion reachesb virt. For example, whenb low = 4andb high = 5,
a virtual precision of 4.05 b corresponds to upgrading the
top 5 % of channel windows in the ranked∆PPLlist to 5-
bit precision. This sensitivity-guided allocation converts the
∆PPLranking into a continuous mixed-precision schedule
that preserves systolic-array regularity while exposing fine-
grained accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. This MPQ mechanism
prioritizes accuracy under a given precision budget, and its
fractional precision profile is fully enabled by FlexPosit’s bit-
serial accelerator, described in the next section.

V. FLEXPOSITBIT-SERIALACCELERATOR
ARCHITECTURE
This section presents the FlexPosit hardware architecture,
which realizes fractional precision tuning while preserving
a fully regular systolic design. The architecture centers on
a variable-precision systolic array orchestrated by a global
precision control unit (GPCU), with a modular hierarchy of
decoder, compute, and rescale units.
A. Variable-Precision Systolic Design
Fig. 6 (a) illustrates the overall FlexPosit architecture.
The design adopts an output-stationary systolic array, where
each weight column integrates a SerialPosit decoder with
lightweight FIFOs, and each row streams FP16 activations
through a grid of MAC clusters. Partial sums accumulate in
the PEs and, after each GEMM tile, drain through per-column
rescale units for dequantization before being written out. This
modular structure supports variable-precision bit-serial weight
streaming without disrupting systolic regularity.
Global Precision Control Unit.At the top level, execution
across the array is orchestrated by a GPCU, which serves
as the temporal backbone of FlexPosit’s variable-precision
design. At the start of each GEMM kernel, the GPCU receives
the target precisionPdetermined by the channel-window-
level precision adaptation, defining aprecision windowofP
cycles representing one complete bit-serial iteration. A small
counter and lightweight control logic generate semantic timing
markers (cyc0,cyc1,cyc2, andcycP), wherecyc0and
cycPdenote the start and end of each window. These markers
coordinate the FSMs of SerialPosit decoders and MAC clus-
ters for global synchronization. The GPCU also governs the
global dataflow schedule, dictating when activations advance
horizontally and when weight terms stream vertically through
the systolic array to maintain precision-synchronous operation.
Dataflow.The FlexPosit dataflow operates under the unified
P-cycle precision window generated by the GPCU, propagated
vertically with each row receiving a one-cycle-shifted ver-
sion of the sequence to maintain continuous bit-serial weight
streaming. As illustrated in Fig. 6(c), the upper row uses
cycletop, while the row below uses the one-cycle–delayed
cycledown, driving each PE’s FSM to capture the correct weight
term and perform the corresponding bit-serial operation with
the current activation. Weights stream bit-serially, are decoded
by the SerialPosit decoders (Section V-C) into four 5-bit terms
per weight, buffered in a per-column FIFO, and consumed by
PEs at the same bit-serial rate. Within each window, activations
advance once while weights propagate bit-serially, one full
weight (four terms) per precision window. This yields fully
synchronized execution across the array without inter-PE FI-
FOs or centralized stall control. Precision changes occur only
at channel-window boundaries, where the GPCU propagates
updated timing semantics with the same one-cycle row skew,
ensuring reconfiguration aligns with the systolic wavefront
without pipeline bubbles.

C. SerialPosit: A Hardware-Friendly Posit
As discussed in Section III, a conventional Posit arithmetic
unit is dominated by wide parallel encoders and decoders
needed to locate the variable-length regime field. Moreover,
maintaining Posit representation across computation stages
incurs additional conversion overhead. De Dinechinet al.[35]
therefore recommend using Posits primarily as a storage
format. Following this philosophy, FlexPosit introducesSerial-
Posit, a hardware-friendly variant that retains Posit’s tapered-
precision advantages while enabling efficient bit-serial decod-
ing of Posit-encoded weights. Posits are used exclusively for
weight storage, and once decoded, all intermediate values are
represented in floating-point format.
Why Bit-serial for Posit?The regime field in a Posit
number is encoded as a run of identical bits terminated by the
opposite bit. Conventional parallel decoders use wide leading-
one/zero detectors to locate this variable-length field in one
cycle [34], [35], increasing area and power cost while fixing
the datapath width. In contrast, a bit-serial pipeline resolves
the regime as bits stream in via a simple XOR of consecutive
bits, making Posit decoding naturally compatible with bit-
serial hardware.
SerialPosit Design.In the original Posit format, two’s-
complement encoding limits efficient bit-serial decoding: for
negative values, the entire word must be two’s-complement
negated before the regime, exponent, and mantissa fields can
be identified. As shown in Fig. 7, SerialPosit is designed
with sign–magnitude encoding instead, where each incoming
bit immediately reflects its field role (sign, regime, exponent,
or mantissa), enabling continuous bit-serial decoding without
waiting for the complete word. This preserves the same
represented value set as Posit(n, es), leaving quantization
behavior unchanged. The trade-off is losing encoded-domain
operations such as direct comparison and negation, which are
unnecessary in this work since Posits are used only for weight
storage and are decoded into the FP-domain datapath before
any arithmetic.

Relation to PIM-based accelerators.FlexPosit tunes
precision by varying bit-serial depth, the number of bit-
positions processed per weight. Processing-in-memory accel-
erators [37]–[39] compute at the bit level within the memory
array, so a channel window’s precision corresponds to how
many bit-planes are activated. Such systems offer high internal
bandwidth for weight access, making them a natural fit for the
proposed precision tuning in future work.
